text:
## Observations

1. Every run of three or more equal elements contains three consecutive equal elements.
2. With one-based indexing, the possible starting positions for a triple are 1 through N − 2, inclusive. When N is 3, there is exactly one candidate.
3. A single matching triple determines the answer, and each candidate takes constant time to check.

## Solution sketch

> Every run of three or more equal elements contains three consecutive equal elements.

1. Read N and store the N integers. For each candidate position i, test whether Aᵢ, Aᵢ₊₁, and Aᵢ₊₂ are all equal. This test also detects longer runs because their first three elements already match.

> With one-based indexing, the possible starting positions for a triple are 1 through N − 2, inclusive. When N is 3, there is exactly one candidate.

2. Scan those positions in order. The final candidate ends at Aₙ, so the scan covers triples at either end of the sequence and checks the single candidate when N is 3.

> A single matching triple determines the answer, and each candidate takes constant time to check.

3. Print `Yes` and stop as soon as a triple matches. If the scan finishes without a match, print `No`. Reading and scanning take O(N) time. The stored sequence uses O(N) space, and the scan uses O(1) additional space.

generation.note: Harness wall time includes Codex startup; not API latency.

usage.note: Codex token counts include its harness context; not comparable to API usage.

isolation.mechanism: codex exec, fresh ephemeral session, empty temporary working directory, user config and exec rules ignored, read-only sandbox, web search and listed features disabled, credential-like variables removed from the environment
isolation.limits: Codex harness instructions and its own tool descriptions remain in the model context; they cannot be removed. Tool isolation is verified post hoc from the event stream, which contained no tool, command, file or search events.
